title: VOCABULARY artifact machine block
description: A VOCABULARY artifact declares one or more named, closed sets of symbols. The envelope is the universal one; everything beyond it is a vocabulary group, whose name is the vocabulary being declared. Envelope keys are excluded from the group pattern by name, so a key is validated as an envelope field or as a vocabulary group, never as both. The surface is closed: a group name must be lower_snake and a group must carry exactly casing, entries and optionally domain_extensible, so nothing undeclared can appear while the set of group names stays open (KV-2, MB-5, MB-11).

authority.description: The authority from which this artifact's jurisdiction derives (CA-1, CA-2). Declared, never inferred from namespace, path or kind.

concern.description: The semantic subject this artifact is about (GO-11, ID-12). A concern classification confers no authority and constitutes no boundary.

extends.description: The vocabulary this one extends, by identity. The empty string is the declared-nothing sentinel: a vocabulary that extends nothing says so rather than omitting the key, because an absent key and a considered 'none' are otherwise indistinguishable (KV-2, and the emptiness-is-declared rule).

^(?!fqdn$)(?!artifact_kind$)(?!version$).description: One declared vocabulary. Its name is the symbol class it governs.

casing.description: The casing every entry conforms to. A closed set, extended by revision.

domain_extensible.description: Whether a domain may add entries. Absent means false: a vocabulary is closed within its revision unless it declares otherwise (KV-2).

entries.description: The declared symbols. An empty vocabulary declares nothing and is refused; emptiness, where meant, is a declared sentinel rather than an absent list.
